0.1: The cost of intelligence falls ten times a year. Demand rises faster. The gap between them is where enterprises win or lose.
0.2: The Akka Agentic AI Platform scales AI efficiently. Let's follow one system from specification to production.
1.1: The platform has four solutions: Akka Specify, the Akka SDK, Akka Verify and Akka Optimize. Specify builds systems from specifications. The Akka SDK runs them. Verify governs them. Optimize runs them on the right models. They share one definition of the system, one runtime and one evidence record.
1.2: The whole system ships as one binary. It scales out under load and recovers on its own when a node fails, with no state lost.
2.1: Our system is a loan origination assistant for a regulated lender. It started as a specification. A coding agent builds it with Akka Specify, and nothing ships until every condition in the spec is met.
2.2: Every condition is checked by a test. When the last one passes, including that a human decides every adverse action, the system is ready to ship. The system is proven against its specification before it is deployed.
3.1: Verify applies controls to any AI system: guardrails, sanitizers, evaluations, policies and people, and records every verdict as evidence against the regulations that apply.
3.2: Here is the system's contract with its regulators: the controls it committed to, signed, and bound to the exact code that enforces them.
3.3: Then the code changes. A developer adds a field the contract never covered. Akka reads the code, sees that the system now handles a protected characteristic, and re-opens the contract.
3.4: The owner confirms it, and the contract adds two controls: an evaluation that checks every decision doesn't rely on that characteristic, and a person who reviews any decision it flags. Version four is signed: immutable, chained to the one before, and verified against trusted keys.
4.1: Every model call goes through Optimize's gateway. Here, the underwriting assistant sends every request to a frontier model.
4.2: Optimize learns from that traffic, trains a small model on the lender's own data, and proposes it. The owner decides whether to try it.
4.3: So it becomes an experiment. The small model answers shadow copies of real requests, then takes a growing share of live traffic, while every limit the owner set is watched.
4.4: In one region, German applications, quality drops below the line. Akka holds the experiment and sends just that region back to the frontier model. The owner chose that, in advance.
4.5: Once it holds everywhere, the owner promotes it. The same answers, at less than a third of the cost, and every step of the decision is on the record.
5.1: And every conversation is captured end to end: what was said, every agent, tool and model call behind it, and every control that judged it, each verdict tied to the contract in force and the regulation it answers. The specification, the code change and the model change are in the same evidence record.
6.1: Every agent, workflow and conversation in Akka is an actor that holds its own state, millions to a core, with no broker, cache or orchestrator around it. As load grows it spreads across the cluster, and latency stays flat.
6.2: So every token, transaction and interaction costs a little less on Akka than on stacks that provision for the peak and meter every call. At a billion interactions, a little becomes a lot: our customers run the same work on a fraction of the cores, hardware and cost.
6.3: Then pair that efficiency with a flat fee. Akka is priced on a platform tier and service cores, not per call or per token, and Optimize keeps token spend inside its forecast. Each interaction costs less, and finance can plan one bill. That is forecastable AI.
6.4: And for sovereign needs, the whole platform runs as a Sovereign Cloud: country-isolated data, networking and operations, in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, T-Systems or Alibaba Cloud.
